title: Durian Stall Ledger
id_line: ID: A | Tier: Beginner | Core topics: basic I/O, loops, 1D arrays, int vs long overflow, exact integer comparison
time_line: Time limit: 1.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
Every evening during durian season, the vendors along the fruit lane near Magsaysay Park in Davao City hand their tally sheets to the city market office. Each stall reports how many kilos of durian it sold and its price per kilo. The market clerk, Inday Lorna, needs three numbers for each market day: the total revenue of the lane, the stall that earned the most, and how many stalls earned strictly more than the average stall. Her old spreadsheet kept printing negative totals on big days, so she asks you for a program that never overflows.
Formally, a market day has N stalls numbered 1 to N. Stall i sold k_i kilos at p_i pesos per kilo, so its revenue is r_i = k_i × p_i.
The total revenue is S = r_1 + r_2 + ... + r_N.
The best stall is the index i with the largest r_i. If several stalls tie, choose the smallest index.
A stall is above average if r_i > S / N, where S / N is the exact (real number) average.
output_format: For each market day print one line with three integers separated by single spaces: S, the index of the best stall, and the number of above-average stalls.
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 100
1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5, and the sum of N over all market days is at most 2 × 10^5
1 ≤ k_i ≤ 10^9
1 ≤ p_i ≤ 10^4

title: Jeepney Signboard Codes
id_line: ID: B | Tier: Beginner | Core topics: string manipulation, run-length encoding, parsing multi-digit numbers, StringBuilder
time_line: Time limit: 1.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
The painters at the Bankerohan jeepney terminal letter route codes onto narrow signboards. Long codes such as AAABCCDDDDDDDDDDDD waste paint, so the terminal adopted a compact notation: every block of repeated letters is written once, followed by how many times it repeats. Dispatchers must also be able to turn a painted code back into the full route code. Write a tool that does both.
Formally, split a string S of uppercase letters into maximal runs of equal consecutive letters. A run consisting of the letter c repeated L times is written as:
c alone, if L = 1;
c followed by the decimal representation of L (no leading zeros), if L ≥ 2.
The encoding of S is the concatenation of the written runs, in order. Decoding is the inverse operation.
output_format: For each of the T lines, print the resulting string on its own line.
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 1000
If op = E: X consists of uppercase letters A to Z, and 1 ≤ |X| ≤ 10^5.
If op = D: X is exactly the encoding of some uppercase string of length between 1 and 10^5. (So adjacent runs in X use different letters, and every written count is at least 2 with no leading zeros.)
The total length of all strings X plus all output strings is at most 10^6.

samples.input:
3
E AAABCCDDDDDDDDDDDD
D A3BC2D12
E XYZ

title: Cooperative Ledger Periods
id_line: ID: C | Tier: Easy to Intermediate | Core topics: prefix sums, HashMap frequency counting, long counters
time_line: Time limit: 1.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
The Toril Farmers' Multi-Purpose Cooperative records the net cash change of its store every day: a positive number is a gain and a negative number is a loss. The board wants to audit on-target periods: blocks of consecutive days whose total net change is exactly the target amount K set at the start of the year. They want to know how many on-target periods exist and how long the longest one is.
Formally, you are given integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_N and K. A pair (l, r) with 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N is an on-target period if a_l + a_(l+1) + ... + a_r = K. Its length is r - l + 1.
input_format: The first line contains N and K. The second line contains N integers a_1, ..., a_N.
output_format: Print two integers separated by a space: the number of on-target periods, and the maximum length of an on-target period (print 0 as the length if there is none).

title: Kadayawan Cup Scoreboard
id_line: ID: D | Tier: Easy to Intermediate | Core topics: simulation, HashMap<String,Integer>, custom Comparator, tie-aware ranking
time_line: Time limit: 2.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
To celebrate the Kadayawan Festival, Davao's universities hold the Kadayawan Cup, an ICPC-style contest. The judges' server crashed just before the awarding, and only the raw submission log survived. You must rebuild the final scoreboard.
There are N teams with distinct names and P problems labeled with the first P uppercase letters. Each log entry has a time in minutes, a team, a problem and a verdict, one of AC, WA, TLE, RTE, CE. The log is in chronological order, and entries with equal time happen in input order.
Scoring rules. For each team and each problem, look at that team's submissions on that problem in log order:
If none of them is AC, the problem is unsolved and contributes nothing (rejected attempts on unsolved problems cost nothing).
Otherwise the problem is solved. Let t be the time of the first AC and w the number of WA, TLE or RTE submissions before that first AC. The problem contributes t + 20 × w penalty minutes. CE submissions are never counted. Every submission after the first AC is ignored.
A team's score is its number of solved problems and its penalty, the sum of the contributions of its solved problems.
Ranking rules. Teams are listed by more solved problems first, then smaller penalty, then team name in increasing lexicographic (ASCII) order. The rank of a team is 1 + the number of teams that solved more problems, or solved the same number with a strictly smaller penalty. (Teams with equal solved and penalty share a rank, and the next rank is skipped, as in 1, 2, 2, 4.)
input_format:
The first line contains N, P and M.
The next N lines each contain one team name.
The next M lines each contain t team problem verdict.
output_format: Print N lines, in ranking order: rank name solved penalty.
constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 10^4, 1 ≤ P ≤ 26, 0 ≤ M ≤ 2 × 10^5
Team names have 1 to 20 characters, each a lowercase letter or a digit, and are distinct.
0 ≤ t ≤ 300, times are non-decreasing; every team in the log is one of the N teams; every problem letter is among the first P letters.

3 3 9
ateneo
usep
jmc
5 jmc A WA
12 jmc A AC
15 usep A AC
20 ateneo B CE
31 ateneo B AC
40 usep B WA
44 jmc B AC
50 usep B AC
60 jmc A WA

4 2 4
delta
alpha
charlie
bravo
10 delta A AC
10 bravo A AC
100 charlie B TLE
200 charlie B RTE

title: The Samal Ferry
id_line: ID: E | Tier: Easy to Intermediate | Core topics: binary search on the answer, greedy feasibility check, long ranges
time_line: Time limit: 1.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
A small passenger ferry runs from the Sasa wharf in Davao City to the Island Garden City of Samal. Passengers wait in a single queue, each with their luggage, and board strictly in queue order. On every trip the ferry takes some passengers from the front of the queue. The cooperative that runs the ferry is buying a new boat and must choose its weight capacity: big boats cost more, so they want the smallest capacity that still gets everyone across today.
Formally, there are N passengers with weights w_1, ..., w_N (luggage included), in queue order. A boat of capacity C (a positive integer) makes trips; each trip carries a group of consecutive passengers from the front of the remaining queue such that:
the total weight of the group is at most C, and
the group has at most P passengers (the number of seats).
The boat may make at most K trips today. Find the minimum integer C for which all N passengers can be carried, or report that no capacity works.
input_format: The first line contains T. Each test case consists of a line with N, K, P, followed by a line with w_1, ..., w_N.
output_format: For each test case print the minimum capacity C, or -1 if it is impossible for every capacity.
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 10
1 ≤ N ≤ 2 × 10^5, and the sum of N over all test cases is at most 2 × 10^5
1 ≤ K ≤ N, 1 ≤ P ≤ N
1 ≤ w_i ≤ 10^9

title: Flash Flood in Matina
id_line: ID: F | Tier: Intermediate | Core topics: multi-source BFS, BFS on grids with time constraints, flattened arrays
time_line: Time limit: 2.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
Heavy rain from the Talomo River floods parts of Barangay Matina. Rescue volunteer Juan is inside a flooded neighborhood and must reach an evacuation point on high ground before the water reaches him. The neighborhood map is a grid of R rows and C columns, where each cell is one of:
. open ground,
# a wall (nobody and no water can enter),
S Juan's starting cell (exactly one; otherwise open ground),
E an evacuation point (high ground: water never enters it),
W a cell that is already flooded at minute 0.
Time advances in whole minutes. Two cells are adjacent if they share a side.
Water. At minute 0 exactly the W cells are flooded. If a cell is flooded at minute m, then at minute m + 1 every adjacent cell that is not # and not E is flooded too. Flooded cells stay flooded.
Juan. Juan is on S at minute 0. Each minute he either stays where he is or moves to an adjacent cell that is not #. Let cell(m) be his cell at minute m. He survives only if cell(m) is not flooded at minute m, for every minute m of his trip. (So he may leave a cell at the same minute water arrives there, but he may never step into a cell that is flooded at the moment of arrival.)
Find the minimum minute m at which Juan can stand on an E cell, or report TRAPPED if he can never reach one.
input_format: The first line contains T. Each test case begins with a line containing R and C, followed by R lines of exactly C characters from .#SEW.
output_format: For each test case print the minimum minute, or the word TRAPPED.
constraints:
1 ≤ T ≤ 10
1 ≤ R, C ≤ 1000, and the sum of R × C over all test cases is at most 10^6
Exactly one S per grid; any number (possibly zero) of E and W cells.

title: Toll Passes over the Davao River
id_line: ID: G | Tier: Upper Intermediate | Core topics: Dijkstra's shortest path, state-expanded (layered) graphs, primitive priority queue
time_line: Time limit: 2.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
A delivery rider for a Davao City food hub must bring an order from barangay 1 to barangay N. The city's road network has N barangays and M two-way roads, and in this (fictional) Davao every road, including the bridges over the Davao River, charges a toll. The hub gives the rider K free passes for the day. Using one pass on a road lets the rider cross it once without paying. Find the minimum total toll the rider must pay.
Formally, road j connects barangays u_j and v_j and costs w_j every time it is traversed (in either direction). A route is a walk from barangay 1 to barangay N. For each traversal in the walk, the rider either pays its toll or spends one pass (making that traversal cost 0); at most K passes may be spent in total. Minimize the total amount paid.
input_format: The first line contains N, M and K. Each of the next M lines contains u_j, v_j and w_j.
output_format: Print the minimum total toll, or -1 if barangay N cannot be reached from barangay 1.
constraints:
2 ≤ N ≤ 10^5, 1 ≤ M ≤ 2 × 10^5, 0 ≤ K ≤ 5
1 ≤ u_j, v_j ≤ N, u_j ≠ v_j; several roads may connect the same pair of barangays
1 ≤ w_j ≤ 10^9

title: SMX Hall Bookings
id_line: ID: H | Tier: Upper Intermediate | Core topics: weighted interval scheduling, 1D DP, sorting primitives, binary search, overflow on time arithmetic
time_line: Time limit: 2.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
The main hall of a convention center in Lanang, Davao City receives N booking requests for the coming year: weddings, tech summits, school proms. Request i occupies the hall from time s_i to time e_i and pays p_i pesos. After each event the crew needs G time units to clean and reset the hall before the next event can start. The manager wants to accept a set of requests with the largest total payment.
Formally, a set of requests is valid if for any two accepted requests i and j with s_i ≤ s_j (and i ≠ j), we have e_i + G ≤ s_j. Find the maximum total payment of a valid set (the empty set is valid and pays 0).
input_format: The first line contains N and G. Each of the next N lines contains s_i, e_i and p_i.

title: The Barangay Health Hub
id_line: ID: I | Tier: Advanced | Core topics: tree DP with rerooting, iterative traversal (no recursion), 64-bit accumulation
time_line: Time limit: 2.0 s | Memory limit: 512 MB
statement:
The provincial health office of Davao de Oro plans to build one vaccine-storage hub in one of its N barangays. The barangays are joined by N - 1 roads that form a tree (there is exactly one simple route between any two barangays). Every resident will travel to the hub once, so the office measures a candidate hub by the total travel distance of all residents. Find the best hub location(s).
Formally, barangay u has population p_u, and road j joins u_j and v_j with length w_j. Let dist(u, h) be the total length of the unique route between u and h. The cost of hub h is
cost(h) = Σ_u p_u × dist(u, h).
Print the minimum cost and every barangay that attains it.
input_format:
The first line contains N.
The second line contains p_1, ..., p_N.
Each of the next N - 1 lines contains u_j, v_j and w_j.
output_format: Print the minimum cost on the first line. On the second line, print all barangays h with cost(h) equal to the minimum, in increasing order, separated by spaces.
constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 2 × 10^5
1 ≤ p_u ≤ 1000
1 ≤ u_j, v_j ≤ N, 1 ≤ w_j ≤ 10^4, and the roads form a tree

title: Agdao Market Price Board
id_line: ID: J | Tier: Advanced | Core topics: segment tree with lazy propagation, (max, count) merging, allocation-free Java, fast I/O at 10^6 scale
time_line: Time limit: 3.0 s | Memory limit: 1024 MB
statement:
The Agdao Public Market shows the price of each of its N fish stalls on a big electronic board. Market news moves prices in blocks: a typhoon warning raises prices for a whole row of stalls, a big catch from the Davao Gulf lowers them. Shoppers often ask the board two questions about a block of stalls: what is the highest price there, and how many stalls charge exactly that much? Your program drives the board.
Formally, you are given a_1, ..., a_N and must process Q operations in order:
1 l r x: add x to every a_i with l ≤ i ≤ r (x may be negative);
2 l r: let M = max(a_l, ..., a_r); print M and the number of indices i in [l, r] with a_i = M.
input_format:
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains a_1, ..., a_N.
Each of the next Q lines contains one operation in the format above.
output_format: For each operation of type 2, print M and the count, separated by a space, on its own line.
constraints:
1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 5 × 10^5
-10^9 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9, -10^9 ≤ x ≤ 10^9
1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N
(Values can drift to about ±5 × 10^14 after many updates.)
